name: portfolio_policy-hold-vs-redeploy
notes: ADR-0279 Stages 1-4 per tax lot: the latest schwab_positions snapshot, and every schwab_transactions trade replayed into open FIFO lots (research A0004), reconciled share for share against it -> liquidation tax per lot by its own holding period; Schwab daily bars -> each symbol's one-year volatility and Blume-adjusted beta against SPY (research A0003) -> risk/{run}.jsonl; market blocks x those betas -> hold returns; an onboarded backtest series -> deflated active hurdle; hold vs redeploy decision per lot -> rows written; the few numbers per lot -> summary/{run}.jsonl. Every rate, horizon, window, premium and field name is a value of THIS document; the kinds carry none. The as_of, rates and returns below are placeholders the owner sets before the first real run; they are the experiment's identity, so changing them changes the hash on purpose. The daily bars snapshot is part of that identity too: the betas it yields price the decision. To fall back to aggregate positions (no lots): delete trades, lots and lot_positions, point tax.inputs.records at $snapshot.records, drop tax.acquired_field AND set summary.key_fields to [account, symbol] (there is no lot_id); in run-decision-outcomes.json set decisions.key_fields to [account, symbol, as_of], outcomes.key_fields to [account, symbol] and drop outcomes.match_fields (tests/test_hold_vs_redeploy.py runs this recipe).

positions.notes: Role 'data': EVERY positions snapshot acquired through dskit.onboarding (connector schwab_positions), one row per account x symbol x day; latest acquisition wins per key. The filter below picks one day.

snapshot.notes: The decision date, declared: one snapshot, so a holding appears once; lots.as_of, tax.as_of, risk_day and risk_latest.reference_date below are pinned to the same day (tests/test_configs.py). Set all five to the day of the pull. Stocks (EQUITY), ETFs (COLLECTIVE_INVESTMENT) and mutual funds (MUTUAL_FUND), as Schwab typed them on the first real pull (2026-10-29): cost_basis is average price x shares, right for all three, while an option contract's multiplier is not applied, so options, and any type not listed, stay out. long_quantity > 0 drops short positions: a short row has a negative market value and basis, and LiquidationTax and HoldVsRedeploy REFUSE such a row by index rather than decide on it, so the owner filters here (a hold-vs-exit decision is about a long holding).

trades.notes: Role 'data': every trade acquired through dskit.onboarding (connector schwab_transactions, source alias schwab_trades: one alias is one connector), one row per account x transaction x symbol: execution time, signed quantity, price, signed net cash. Only VALID transactions arrive (the connector refuses a PENDING or INVALID one). The pull's start must reach back to the earliest purchase still held, or the reconciliation in lot_positions refuses.

lots.notes: Open lots per account x symbol as of the snapshot day (pinned equal to snapshot.where[as_of] and tax.as_of by tests/test_configs.py): every trade up to it, that day's included, replayed in day, execution time, transaction id order (order_fields: a same-day buy precedes the sell that closes it whatever the ids), a sell taking the earliest lots first (fifo, the rule when no lot is identified; Schwab's default for stocks, while funds and some ETFs in accounts opened before October 2024 default to average cost: confirm the account's election). A buy's basis is the cash it paid (amount, fees included) or quantity x price when the amount is null (a transaction with several kept items; the summary's amount_fallbacks counts them). Wash sales are not modelled (a disallowed loss would raise the new lot's basis and tack the old holding period); they, average cost and specific-lot elections show as a lot_positions basis_gap. allow_incomplete true: Schwab's transactions history began in 2024 on the first real pull, so most holdings predate it; a holding the history cannot account for (bought before the pull's start, transferred in, sold short) withholds its lots and lot_positions falls back to its aggregate row (Schwab's basis, a null acquired date, taxed as default_holding). A holding mixing older shares with later buys falls back whole, so its recent shares are taxed as default_holding too. false refuses by name instead. Pinned equal to lot_positions.allow_incomplete.

lot_positions.notes: Each lot becomes a position row: long_quantity = the lot's shares, market_value = its share of the position's value at the snapshot's price, cost_basis = the lot's basis, plus lot_id and acquired. Every snapshot holding must reconcile: its lots' shares equal its long_quantity within tolerance (0.0 shares; raise it to a few thousandths only if dividend reinvestment rounding differs between the two endpoints). A holding that does not reconcile, or has no lots, refuses unless allow_incomplete, when it passes through as its aggregate row with a null acquired date (default_holding applies). The summary's basis_gap per holding is lot basis - Schwab's cost basis: zero when fifo matches the account's books, and basis_gap_max (the largest |gap|, logged as a warning when beyond float noise) is the one number to check on the first real run.

tax.notes: One row per lot. as_of equals the snapshot day above (tests/test_configs.py pins it with lots.as_of and the two risk dates), so the holding period is measured to the day the positions were taken whatever --asof labels the run. Each lot is long when held at least long_term_days (366: more than a year, exact except when the year spans 29 February) and short otherwise; an aggregate fallback row (null acquired) takes default_holding. Rates are the owner's marginal federal + NIIT placeholders; state tax is not included.

market.notes: Role 'data': the market's expected nominal return from four public numbers (research A0001): S&P 500 dividend yield, long-run real earnings growth, expected inflation, and the drift from today's Shiller CAPE toward a fair CAPE over reversion_years. horizon_years is the decision's horizon (tests/test_configs.py pins it equal to decide.horizon_years) and may not exceed reversion_years: the drift is spread over reversion_years, and a longer horizon would compound it past full reversion. Placeholders; the owner refreshes them from public data before each real run.

bars.notes: Role 'data': every closed daily session acquired through dskit.onboarding (connector schwab_daily), one row per symbol x session date (ts, YYYY-MM-DD); the latest acquisition wins per key, so a corrected close replaces the first. The source's symbols are the held symbols plus the benchmark SPY, and its start is at least 400 calendar days before the decision day: 252 returns need 253 closes.

benchmark.notes: The market the betas are measured against: SPY's own daily bars from the same pull, so both sides of the regression are price returns on one basis (research A0003).

risk_features.notes: Per symbol and session (research A0003): the zero-mean root mean square of the last 252 daily log returns (one year, not yet annualized) and the OLS beta of those returns on SPY's over the same 252 sessions (rolling covariance over rolling variance). Null until a symbol has 253 closes. close_field and benchmark_close_field are both the CLOSE (pinned by tests/test_configs.py): every return is close to close, the holding's and SPY's on one basis. The windows count a symbol's own consecutive bars, not calendar days: a session missing from the pull merges two days into one return, so 252 returns then span more than a year (one missing session stretches the window by one session; SPY missing a day a holding has nulls that return and so every beta window holding it).

risk_day.notes: Nothing after the decision day: the same day as snapshot.where[as_of], lots.as_of, tax.as_of and risk_latest.reference_date (tests/test_configs.py pins the five). <= and not ==: a daily candle is closed only once its New York date has passed, so a pull on the decision day itself has no bar for that day; risk_latest takes each symbol's latest session on or before it.

risk_latest.notes: One row per symbol: its latest session on or before the decision day and that session's trailing numbers; as_of is carried to risk/{run}.jsonl. Staleness gate: reference_date is the decision day (the same day as risk_day, snapshot, lots and tax; pinned by tests/test_configs.py) and max_lag_days 5 is CALENDAR days, a bound that covers the longest closure a healthy feed shows (Friday to a Tuesday after a holiday Monday is 4 days) with a day to spare. A symbol whose latest session is more than 5 days before the decision day, or after it, stops the run by name with its latest session and lag, so a stale pull (a symbol dropped from the source, a pull not refreshed) is never priced silently.

risk.notes: annual_vol = the daily RMS x sqrt(252), 252 being trading days a year (not the window, which happens to equal it). beta = beta_raw - 0.33 x (beta_raw - 1) = 0.67 x raw + 0.33, the Blume adjustment (Bloomberg's adjusted beta): a third of the way to 1, the forecast that prices the hold return; beta_raw stays beside it (research A0003). vol_window and beta_window restate risk_features' windows for the reader, as integers (`integer`, not `const`, which computes in floats and would write 252.0), pinned equal by tests/test_configs.py. A symbol without a full window has nulls here, and betas / summary refuse it by name.

vols.notes: {symbol: annual volatility}, the summary's volatilities table.

risk_betas.notes: {symbol: adjusted beta}, wired into betas: what prices each holding's hold return.

params.source: risk inputs per symbol from Schwab daily bars

risks.notes: Role 'report': one row per symbol in ./risk under the invoking cwd, one file per run (ADR-0247): symbol, as_of (the session read), daily_vol, beta_raw, annual_vol, beta and the two windows (integers).

betas.notes: risk_free + beta x (market - risk_free) per symbol, each holding's beta wired from the risk chain (its Blume-adjusted one-year daily beta against SPY, research A0003); there is no hand table. A holding missing from the bars, or without a full year of them, refuses by name, on purpose: no default_beta here, so a new position cannot be silently priced as the market.

active_returns.notes: Role 'data': the per-period NET returns of the active strategy the cash would go to, onboarded from a child's scored backtest (one jsonl row per period: period, net_return) through localfiles. Data enters through onboarding, so the series the hurdle is built on is a WORM snapshot with a digest, not a pasted number.

hurdle.notes: Stage 3: (mean - E[max null Sharpe] x sd) x periods, the return left once what selection alone would have found is removed. trials is the owner's honest count of strategy variants tried; min_dsr is the pre-registered admissibility bar — below it the hurdle is withheld and every holding holds. min_periods is the fewest weekly returns the backtest may carry: 52 is one year; a shorter series refuses by name. Returns are fractions (0.01 = 1%): a percent series annualizes outside [-1, 2] and refuses.

decide.notes: Both returns come wired: hold from $betas.rates, redeploy from $hurdle.rate (None when inadmissible -> hold). No return literal exists in this node. redeploy_cost is a cost charged on top of the backtest's returns, which are already net of whatever costs the backtest itself charged: set it to 0 if the backtest netted its costs, or the active path is charged twice. risk_premium 0.0 is a placeholder, NOT a claim that zero is safe: the hurdle is deflated for selection, but its arithmetic mean compounds geometrically here, so the simple-vs-geometric gap (about sd^2/2 per year) is left to risk_premium. The owner should set it from the backtest's annual volatility (hurdle summary annual_sd) before a real run. Taxes differ by path on purpose: the hold path realizes its gain once at the horizon at the long-term rate over the original basis; the active path turns over, so it pays the short-term rate every year (annual timing) and owes nothing at the end. Net to net.

params.source: hold-vs-redeploy decisions per account x symbol x lot

decisions.notes: Role 'report': the advisory rows, one per lot (lot_id, acquired), with liq_* and the decision, in ./decisions under the invoking cwd, one file per run so no run shadows another (ADR-0247). Never an order. Lots of one holding may decide differently: a young lot pays the short-term rate to sell, an old one the long-term rate.

summary.notes: The few numbers (research A0002), one row per lot (key_fields carry lot_id; concentration still merges by symbol; the metrics' positions, exit_positions and hold_positions count LOTS, not holdings): per lot its weight, expected return a year, volatility, beta, embedded gain and tax cost of selling as shares of value, the break-even active return at which exiting ties holding, and the after-tax opportunity cost of holding a year (above zero: exit wins); the portfolio's totals, weighted return and beta, concentration by symbol (HHI, top weight) and aggregate opportunity cost in its metrics output. The portfolio's embedded gain nets losses across holdings, but its tax cost nets them only when tax.loss_offset is true; while it is false a loss offsets no gain and the tax cost errs high. The field names and the four redeploy terms restate decide's, pinned equal by tests/test_configs.py, so the break-even inverts exactly the comparison decide made. betas is wired from the beta table that priced the hold return. volatilities is wired from the risk chain: each symbol's one-year annual volatility from Schwab daily bars, the same for every lot of a symbol.

params.source: position summary per account x symbol x lot

summaries.notes: Role 'report': one summary row per lot in ./summary under the invoking cwd, one file per run (ADR-0247). The portfolio numbers are the summary node's metrics: carry.json in the run directory holds them and `python -m dskit.pipeline runs` tabulates them run over run.

outputs.notes: Empty = ./pipeline_runs under the invoking cwd. Placement is not identity.
